reference_drawer.title: 📖 Zeroes & Coefficients Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Standard Quadratic Identities and Vieta's Relations for ax² + bx + c:

items.rule: Sum of zeroes equals negative of (coefficient of x) divided by (coefficient of x²).
Product of zeroes equals (constant term) divided by (coefficient of x²).
A quadratic polynomial with given sum S and product P of zeroes is given by k(x² - Sx + P).
Sum of squares of zeroes expressed via sum and product.

concepts.title: 1. Standard Quadratic Form & Coefficients
concepts.subtitle: Identifying a, b, and c
concepts.summary: Every quadratic polynomial can be written in standard form p(x) = ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0.

points.text: a: Coefficient of x² (must not be zero).
b: Coefficient of x (includes its preceding sign).

concepts.trap: Always rearrange terms in descending powers of x (e.g. 6x² - 3 - 7x must be rewritten as 6x² - 7x - 3).

concepts.title: 2. Sum of Zeroes Relation
concepts.subtitle: The -b/a Relationship
concepts.summary: If α and β are zeroes of ax² + bx + c, their sum is always equal to -b/a.

points.text: Formula: α + β = -(coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x²).
Sign Caution: The formula has an intrinsic negative sign: -b/a. If b is negative, -b becomes positive.

concepts.trap: Forgetting the minus sign when b is already negative.

concepts.title: 3. Product of Zeroes Relation
concepts.subtitle: The c/a Relationship
concepts.summary: If α and β are zeroes of ax² + bx + c, their product is always equal to c/a.

points.text: Sign Rule: The sign of c is preserved directly.

concepts.trap: Dividing by b instead of leading coefficient a.

concepts.title: 4. Forming a Quadratic Polynomial from Zeroes
concepts.subtitle: Reconstructing p(x) from Sum and Product
concepts.summary: A quadratic polynomial with sum of zeroes S and product of zeroes P is given by p(x) = k(x² - Sx + P).

points.text: Non-zero constant k: Used to clear denominators if S or P are fractional.

concepts.trap: Writing x² + Sx + P instead of x² - Sx + P.

concepts.title: 5. Symmetric Expressions in α and β
concepts.subtitle: Evaluating Values Without Finding Roots
concepts.summary: Expressions symmetric in α and β can be evaluated directly using only (α + β) and (αβ).
concepts.trap: Do not attempt to solve for individual radical roots; rewrite the expression in terms of S and P.

concepts.title: 6. Forming Polynomials with Transformed Zeroes
concepts.subtitle: Roots like α², β² or 1/α, 1/β
concepts.summary: To form a new polynomial whose roots are transformed versions of α and β, compute the new sum S' and new product P' using (α + β) and (αβ).

points.text: New Sum S': For roots α² and β², compute S' = α² + β² = (α + β)² - 2αβ.
New Product P': For roots α² and β², compute P' = α²β² = (αβ)².
New Polynomial: Substitute S' and P' into p(x) = k(x² - S'x + P').

concepts.trap: Do not attempt to find individual roots α and β; always express S' and P' in terms of (α + β) and (αβ).
